phrases.english_text: As for me, one time, I still remember us Cherokee speakers sitting on one side and the English speakers on the other side. The teacher would ask one girl to pass out papers to us. We just all looked at each other. “What is this?” we all thought. It was written in English. We would sit there all that time watching the white kids writing. Still, we asked each other, “What are we supposed to be doing?” – “I don’t know” we’d say. Then the teacher picked up the papers, and we’d give them to her with nothing written on it. Finally, she realized … Her [Elsie] mom, she raised me. Her niece was working in the kitchen and could speak good Cherokee and English. The teacher went and asked her, “I told them, you all don’t understand English. That’s why they didn’t write anything, they don’t know how to read.” She came and helped us, the cook. She taught us English.

phrases.english_text: Do you all read and write Cherokee?

Yeah, I learned it. When was it? When we lived behind the school. One time, I wasn’t there. Anyway, when I got there, “Hey, you have to go down the hill to another building to take a test. If you don’t pass it, you won’t get your certificate," they told me. So, the lady that worked with me, we went down there. “Me, I’m going to go there, but I can’t pass it, because I didn’t know how to read and write.” Because I really didn’t know back then. Anyway, I got there and I told the other woman, “I’m just gonna sit here and wait for you.” – Anyway, “I’m going to pray,” I said. “I’m going to pray real hard,” I told her. So, I prayed and asked God to help me. I told Him, “I don’t know how to read and write.” I prayed for about ten minutes. There was nothing written in front of the paper we were to fill out with syllabary. “If you don’t fill it out, then you won’t pass,” they said. I went and sat down, and the Lord just put everything in front of me. I wrote out the whole syllabary chart. I did this for the next page. I had to read it. You had to write it in English, and also the syllabary, about pages worth. The last page I had to read. Anyway, I just felt funny sitting there writing and I had to read it. “Alright. Thank you, Lord,” I said. I turned in the test paper. Then they called me in. “You did well,” she said. I looked at her, it was Bobbie Smith and Ana [Sixkiller]. They were the ones giving the test. I got 95%. I said, “Oh my gosh! Thank you, Lord!” I said. “What happened to the other 5%?” I asked her. “You went over ten minutes reading it,” she told me. I read it, but I didn’t really know how. That’s when it started, me reading well. I was really glad. If you really believe, the Lord will help you if you ask Him.

phrases.english_text: Yeah, they live up on the hill. We lived up there for a while, when the house that we grew up in burned. I couldn’t fix it like the way they had it, I was just standing there, “Haw!” I was saying.
